## explicitness

Hop marks carried from blind_answer: H1, H2, H3, H4, H6 read off (all from the same document); H5 partly read off. Whole-corpus read (75 docs) plus a mechanical n-gram check against the yaml (no charter copy of 11+ tokens; 8-token overlaps are fixed phrases and table rows) and a keyword sweep for gating language ("before / first / only after / until / not yet / then / relies on / depend"): every dependency-bearing hit lies in doc_dg_amended_declaration_review_c84489cb; the tool documents' "unlocks it first … then calls it" concern the unlock/call mechanics of one tool, not an order between problems.

**KB-EXPLICIT RED — EX0-1 … EX0-5 (all in doc_dg_amended_declaration_review_c84489cb).**

- EX0-1 — task-mirroring title. "Dangerous Goods Acceptance: Gross Weight Amendments on a File Awaiting Decision" names the situation task 0 presents (weight amendment on an undecided file), not a general subject; it is the rendering of the workflow `scenario`.
- EX0-2 — opening describes the particular combination of circumstances. "## The situation this account covers — Dangerous Goods Acceptance regularly meets a file that is under review and has not been decided, whose cargo cut-off has not passed, and whose shipper needs the declared gross weight changed through a signed amendment while the review is still open. The matter is settled when three things are true together: every fee the undecided file owes is on its account, the acceptance carries the amended weight, and the outcome of the review, together with any administration fee an approval brings, is recorded against the sailing of the booking." — states the terminal state of the procedure and frames it for exactly the caller's situation.
- EX0-3 — workflow parts listed, surfacing the hidden problems. "## The parties and what each part achieves" — three bullets: the shipper signs the amended declaration; "**The desk, on the account.** The desk enters the late declaration fee where the initial declaration was accepted despite a late signature, and the amendment fee that the signed amendment gives rise to."; "**The desk, on the decision.**". This names both unasked problems (the late declaration fee the caller never mentions, the second amendment fee) as parts of this situation, so neither has to be discovered from the decision principles and the records.
- EX0-4 — dependencies and order stated outright. "## What each part relies on": "**The amendment charge relies on the signature.** … Where the shipper has signed nothing, there is no amendment to name and nothing to charge." (H2); "**The decision relies on a square account.** The decision is given on a file whose account reflects the amendment charges its signed amendments call for and the late charge its initial declaration calls for." (H1, H3); "A late charge is also one that only an undecided file can receive; a decided file is out of its reach." (H4); "**The decision ends the review.**" (decision last); "**The late charge does not depend on the amendment.** … Its place relative to the signature is a matter of convention, not of necessity." (H6). Together these are the workflow's order_rationale in prose: the whole order is readable without combining any other sentence or record. The semantics each carries is correct and must remain entailed (it already is, by the home documents listed under source_to_kb) — the finding is only that it is stated.
- EX0-5 — copied workflow wording and an outright act-now answer. "## Timing … Nothing waits for an inspection, a delivery, a payment to clear, an outside approval, a batch run or the passage of time." is a near-verbatim copy of the workflow's zero_wait_proof ("No step waits for an inspection, a delivery, a payment clearing, an external approval, a batch run or the passage of time."), and the section tells the solver outright that every part is done within the one conversation.
